Land and Environment

Kiswahili: Ardhi na Mazingira

Classifies land into public, community, and private categories. Mandates equitable access, security of land rights, sustainable management, and elimination of gender discrimination in land law.

Key constitutional takeaways

  • •Land is held, used, and managed equitably, efficiently, productively, and sustainably.
  • •Classification into public land, community land, and private land.
  • •Obligation to maintain at least ten percent tree cover across Kenya.

Articles in Chapter 5

Select an article to read its legal clauses and plain language meaning.

Clauses

(1)Land in Kenya shall be held, used and managed in a manner that is equitable, efficient, productive and sustainable, and in accordance with the following principles- (a) equitable access to land; (b) security of land rights; (c) sustainable and productive management of land resources; (d) transparent and cost effective administration of land; (e) sound conservation and protection of ecologically sensitive areas; (f) elimination of gender discrimination in law, customs and practices related to land and property in land; and (g) encouragement of communities to settle land disputes through recognised local community initiatives consistent with this Constitution.
(2)These principles shall be implemented through a national land policy developed and reviewed regularly by the national government and through legislation.

In plain language

Guarantees equal land ownership rights for women and protects ancestral community lands.
